help.intro: AI research tests a business judgement with AI-simulated respondents. You write the question; the AI clarifies the goal with you, reads public sources, designs the study, interviews each persona and writes a report in which every finding cites its quotes.
help.label: Guide
help.more: Type @ in the conversation to cite this study's report, personas and interviews. Report templates (top right of the research home) set the report layout; new studies use the selected template.
help.outputs: Report holds the findings; Hypotheses shows how well each claim is supported; Personas, Interviews and Discussion hold what the AI-simulated respondents said; Analysis and Files are supporting material. Share sends the study to your team, and the share page also states that respondents are AI-simulated.
help.personas: A persona is the profile an AI-simulated respondent plays. Build one in the persona library by chatting, filling in a form, or uploading interview notes or survey data, then reuse it in new studies with "Pick from library". Personas do not represent real customers.
help.settings: The method sets the question framework: JTBD asks which job users hire a product for, KANO separates must-haves from delighters. More respondents broaden coverage; interview depth controls how closely answers are explored. Interviews stop when sufficient, with at most 20 rounds each. When unsure, leave them on Auto and the AI will choose.
help.simulated: All respondents are simulated by AI from personas; they are not real users. Use AI research to narrow the field and find hypotheses worth testing before real research, not to replace it. Reports say "most / some / few" and make no statistical claims.
help.subtitle: The flow, outputs and limits of AI research
help.summary: Test business judgements with AI-simulated respondents. Click for the full guide.
help.title: AI research guide
help.validation: AI findings need real people to check them. Validation holds a questionnaire for real customers (exportable as CSV for survey tools). Upload the answers to the conversation and the AI compares them with the simulated findings, marking where they agree and conflict.
